summary.one_liner: A curated, categorized list of links to articles and a few libraries about falsehoods programmers commonly believe, such as assumptions about email addresses, time, names, Unicode and addresses.
summary.what_it_does: This is an "awesome" style link list rather than a software project. It collects articles, talks and some code resources that each explain a set of false assumptions developers often hold, with a one-line description for each entry. The entries are grouped into topic sections such as Dates and Time, Emails, Human Identity, Internationalization, Postal Addresses, Phone Numbers, Networks, Web and Software Engineering. A few entries point to libraries or datasets, such as libphonenumber, libaddressinput, libvldmail, i18n Testing Data and the Big List of Naughty Strings, marked as free. The README describes the list as covering falsehoods, not as providing code, and has a contribution section for adding entries.
use_cases: Finding the classic 'Falsehoods Programmers Believe' articles
Checking assumptions about time zones, DST and calendars
Learning why email and name validation rules are harder than expected
Finding Unicode and character encoding pitfalls to read up on
Locating test data and naughty strings for input testing
Reviewing edge cases before designing addresses, phone numbers or payments
notable: Organized by topic into about 20 sections, from Arts to Web
Each entry has a short description of the falsehood it covers
Includes a few free libraries and datasets, such as libphonenumber and Big List of Naughty Strings, marked in the list
Linked from other curated lists such as kuchin/awesome-cto and charlax/professional-programming
caveats: Contains links only, so the content lives on external sites that may change or disappear
The README does not state a license
Some entries are videos or talks, not written text
